newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian official says U.S. stand "disgraceful".
newsitem.headline: Palestinian official says U.S. stand "disgraceful".

text.p: Palestinian Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo on Sunday called U.S. policy on peace negotiations between the Palestinian Authority and Israel "disgraceful".

"As far as the U.S. is concerned, its position is disgraceful and it has proved until now that they join Israel in disrespecting the Oslo accords," Abed Rabbo told Reuters, referring to the landmark 1993 interim Israeli-Palestinian peace accord.
That accord was reached by Israel's previous government. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who opposed the accord when in opposition, ousted the prior government in elections a year ago.

Abed Rabbo also said, in a statement released later on Sunday, that the Palestinian Authority demanded formation of an "international supervisory committee" on Jewish settlement of lands Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war.
The committee would include Jordan and Egypt -- Arab states already at peace with Israel -- and the United States, the European Union and Russia.
"The Palestinian Authority is demanding the formation of an international supervisory committee...to save the peace process," the statement said.
The Authority has urged Washington to pressure Israel to halt expansion of Jewish settlements in lands Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war, especially in East Jerusalem.
The United States has said both sides must make tough decisions to revive the peacemaking that was plunged into crisis when Israel began a new 6,500-home settlement in East Jerusalem on March 18.
Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak is to meet Netanyahu at the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh on Tuesday in hopes of finding a way to revive peace talks.
